title: Testable Script Architecture knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Testable Script Architecture”?
options: Quoting local and remote command arguments
Separating side effects from decision logic
questions.answer_key: Separating side effects from decision logic
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Separating side effects from decision logic” under lesson 162, “Testable Script Architecture”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Testable Script Architecture”?
options: Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
questions.answer_key: Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review.
questions.explanation: Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Testable Script Architecture”?
options: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
